case.title: Joseph Chidubem Nwachukwu v. Mainstreet Bank Limited

procedural_history.originating_proceedings: Complaint dated and filed on 28th November 2011.
procedural_history.procedural_posture: Claimant filed complaint, statement of facts, list of witness, list of exhibits and copies of exhibits (Exhibits A–H). By order of Court made on 22nd March 2012, parties were asked to file and serve sworn depositions of witnesses. Claimant filed deposition on 24th April 2012, later amended statement of facts and witness deposition on 19th June 2012, and further amended statement of facts and further deposition on 7th January 2013. Additional documents (Exhibits I–N) filed. Defendant entered appearance by filing memorandum of appearance but did not file defence until 28th March 2013. Defendant made only two appearances in Court (21st February 2012 and 22nd March 2012) and was absent throughout trial despite service of hearing notices. Court permitted claimant to argue its case in the absence of the defendant.
interlocutory_applications: Claimant applied for leave to amend statement of facts and witness deposition on oath; granted on 19th June 2012.
Claimant again applied for leave to amend statement of facts and deposition on oath; granted; claimant filed 2nd amended statement of facts and further deposition on 7th January 2013.
procedural_events: Order of Court on 22nd March 2012 for parties to file sworn depositions.
Leave granted on 19th June 2012 to amend statement of facts and witness deposition.
Defendant filed statement of defence and other processes on 28th March 2013.
Trial commenced with claimant testifying as CW; defendant absent.

material_facts: Claimant was employed by defendant Bank (formerly International Bank for West Africa Ltd and Afribank Nigeria Plc, now Mainstreet Bank Ltd) as a Copy Typist starting from 13th January 1981 via letter of appointment dated 9th April 1981 (Exhibit A).
Employment was confirmed by letter dated 19th October 1981 (Exhibit B).
Claimant was promoted to Senior Assistant Manager by letter dated 19th November 2007 (Exhibit C).
As Senior Assistant Manager, claimant became a member of ASSBIFI and paid dues (Exhibits I, J, K, L, M, N).
Claimant received letter dated 22nd June 2010 (Exhibit G) summarily dismissing him with immediate effect, stating 'your services are no longer required in the Bank'.
The dismissal letter was signed by Tolu Ilori and Babs Ogunleye.
Claimant's conditions of service incorporated the collective agreement (Exhibit D) by virtue of Exhibit A.
Article 4(iv)(c) of Part II (section 1) of Exhibit D requires a written query and opportunity to defend before summary dismissal, except where employee absconded.
No evidence that claimant absconded or was given a written query before dismissal.
Claimant was a financial member of ASSBIFI as evidenced by pay-slips (Exhibits I, J, K, L).

chronology.event: Claimant commenced employment as Copy Typist.
Claimant promoted to Senior Assistant Manager (Exhibit C).
Claimant summarily dismissed via letter (Exhibit G).

background_facts: Defendant Bank formerly known as International Bank for West Africa Ltd and Afribank Nigeria Plc, now Mainstreet Bank Ltd by order of Central Bank of Nigeria.
Claimant's employment governed by collective agreement (Exhibit D) between ASSBIFI and NEABIA.
facts.employment_relationship: Claimant was an employee of the defendant Bank from 13th January 1981 until summary dismissal on 22nd June 2010, serving 29 years.
facts.contractual_relationship: Employment contract incorporated collective agreement (Exhibit D) as part of terms and conditions of service.
documentary_evidence: Exhibit A: Letter of appointment dated 9th April 1981.
Exhibit B: Letter confirming appointment dated 19th October 1981.
Exhibit C: Promotion letter dated 19th November 2007.
Exhibit G: Summary dismissal letter dated 22nd June 2010.
Exhibit H: Statement of Account of Retirement Savings with Trust Fund.
Exhibits I, J, K, L: Pay-slips evidencing payment of ASSBIFI membership dues.
witness_evidence: Claimant testified as CW and tendered Exhibits A–N. Defendant did not cross-examine CW.

causes_of_action: Failure to give notice or salary in lieu

claims.claim: Declaration that summary dismissal is wrongful, null and void.
claims.legal_basis: Breach of collective agreement and conditions of service.

claims.claim: Order changing summary dismissal to termination.
Payment of N1,624,926.66 being 3 months' salary in lieu of notice as damages.
Payment of N33,073,597.52 being terminal benefits (16 weeks of total emoluments for each completed year of service, 29 years).
Payment of current pension savings held by Trustfund.
Payment of retirement contributions held by defendant.

reliefs_sought.relief: Declaration that summary dismissal vide letter dated June 22, 2010, ref. HCM/IRSW/24224/2010 is wrongful, null and void.
Order changing summary dismissal to termination.
Order directing defendant to pay N1,624,926.66 being 3 months' salary in lieu of notice as damages.
Order directing defendant to pay N33,073,597.52 being terminal benefits (16 weeks of total emoluments for each completed year of service, 29 years).
Order directing current pension savings held by Trustfund be paid to claimant.
Order directing retirement contributions held by defendant be paid to claimant.

issues_for_determination.issue: Whether from the totality of evidence, unchallenged, claimant is entitled to judgment.
Whether from totality of evidence, claimant proved his case to entitle him to judgment.

questions_of_law: Whether 'your services are no longer required' is a reason for dismissal or the act of dismissal.
Whether employer must state reasons for termination or dismissal.
Whether failure to comply with disciplinary procedure in collective agreement renders dismissal null and void.

claimant_arguments: Defendant did not file defence or cross-examine CW, so evidence is unchallenged and deemed admitted.
Burden of proof is minimal where evidence is unchallenged.
Summary dismissal was wrongful as it violated collective agreement (Exhibit D) which requires query and opportunity to defend before dismissal.
The reason 'services no longer required' is not a ground for summary dismissal under the collective agreement.
Claimant is entitled to terminal benefits, pension, and retirement contributions.
submissions: Claimant submitted that unchallenged evidence requires minimal proof, citing Kosile v. Folarin and Nigerian Bottling Company Plc v. Abubakar.
Claimant submitted that collective agreement incorporated into contract of employment must be followed, citing Planned Parenthood Federation of Nigeria v. Shogbola and Tomlirison v. Lmssr.

party_authorities.proposition: Where evidence is unchallenged, onus of proof is discharged on minimum proof.

The Registered Trustees of the Planned Parenthood Federation of Nigeria & anor v. Dr. Jimmy Shogbola [2005] 1 WRN 15
party_authorities.proposition: Collective agreement incorporated into contract must be followed; breach renders termination wrongful.
Steps in collective agreement for determination must be followed.

evidential_findings.finding: Claimant was a financial member of ASSBIFI and his conditions of service governed by collective agreement.
Claimant was summarily dismissed without query or opportunity to defend.

findings_of_fact.finding: Claimant was a financial member of ASSBIFI.
No evidence that claimant was given written query or opportunity to defend before dismissal.
The phrase 'your services are no longer required' is the act of dismissal, not the reason.

findings_of_law.finding: Employer need not state reasons for termination or dismissal.

findings_of_law.issue: Effect of non-compliance with collective agreement
findings_of_law.finding: Dismissal not in accordance with conditions of service is wrongful, unlawful, null and void.
Collective agreement provides for one month's salary in lieu of notice, not three months.

judicial_analysis.reasoning: The Court found that the claimant's employment was governed by the collective agreement (Exhibit D) which required a written query and opportunity to defend before summary dismissal. The defendant failed to comply. The dismissal was therefore wrongful, unlawful, null and void. The Court distinguished between termination and dismissal, noting dismissal carries infamy. The Court held that the claimant was entitled to reliefs 1 and 2, and to one month's salary in lieu of notice as per the collective agreement. Reliefs 4, 5, and 6 were deemed abandoned for lack of proof.

issue_analysis.issue: Whether the summary dismissal was wrongful, null and void.

arguments.claimant: Dismissal violated collective agreement as no query or opportunity to defend was given; reason 'services no longer required' not a ground for summary dismissal.

issue_analysis.judicial_analysis: The Court found that the collective agreement (Exhibit D) was incorporated into the contract of employment. Article 4(iv)(c) required a written query and opportunity to defend before summary dismissal. No evidence of compliance. The dismissal was therefore not in accordance with the conditions of service.
issue_analysis.holding: Summary dismissal is wrongful, null and void.
issue_analysis.ratio_decidendi: Where a collective agreement incorporated into a contract of employment prescribes a disciplinary procedure, failure to comply renders the dismissal null and void.

issue_analysis.issue: Whether summary dismissal should be changed to termination.

arguments.claimant: Dismissal should be converted to termination to remove infamy and allow terminal benefits.

issue_analysis.judicial_analysis: The Court noted the distinction between dismissal and termination. Dismissal carries infamy and deprives terminal benefits. Since the dismissal was wrongful, it should be changed to termination.
issue_analysis.ratio_decidendi: A wrongful dismissal may be converted to termination to mitigate the opprobrium and allow terminal benefits.

issue_analysis.issue: Whether claimant is entitled to 3 months' salary in lieu of notice.

arguments.claimant: Entitled to 3 months' salary in lieu of notice as per terms of employment.

issue_analysis.judicial_analysis: The Court examined Exhibit D and found that Article 4(ii)(d) provides for one month's notice or salary in lieu, not three months. The claimant's claim for three months was not supported by the collective agreement.
issue_analysis.holding: Claimant entitled to one month's salary in lieu of notice, not three months.
issue_analysis.ratio_decidendi: Entitlement to notice period is governed by the express terms of the collective agreement.
issue_analysis.result: Relief 3 partially granted; awarded N541,642.22 (one month's salary).

holdings.holding: Summary dismissal is wrongful, null and void.
Claimant entitled to one month's salary in lieu of notice.

ratio_decidendi.principle: Where a collective agreement incorporated into a contract of employment prescribes a disciplinary procedure, failure to comply renders the dismissal null and void.
ratio_decidendi.application: Defendant failed to give written query and opportunity to defend before summary dismissal.

ratio_decidendi.principle: Entitlement to notice period is governed by the express terms of the collective agreement.
ratio_decidendi.application: Collective agreement provided for one month's salary in lieu of notice, not three months.
ratio_decidendi.holding: Claimant entitled to one month's salary in lieu of notice.
